text.p: The Russian government expects to decide how to divide its 24 percent stake in the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) within a month, deputy energy minister Viktor Ott said on Friday.
"There is a proposal for handing over management of the government share (in CPC)," Ott said after the signing ceremony of the CPC agreement. "It will be within the next month," he added.

Russia has a 24 percent stake in the $2 billion oil pipeline project. The group will build a 1,500-km (940 mile) pipeline from the huge Tengiz field in Kazakhstan to Russia's Black Sea oil export outlet of Novorossiisk.
A final agreement on the project was signed on Friday, allowing full project financing and construction to proceed, the CPC said.

Ott said the share was now under the control of the Russian Federal Property Fund, and that there was a proposal to divide the share equally between state oil company Rosneft, Russia's largest oil company LUKoil LKOH.RTS and Transneft, the monopoly pipeline operator.
But he could not confirm whether such a proposal would be adopted.
A CPC source said the group understood that the government share would be managed jointly by the three parties.

The question of whether Transneft gets a share in the government stake has been a sticking point during talks, because some CPC members said it could present a conflict of interest with Transneft's possible role as pipeline operator.
But consortium members played down the significance of who might control the government stake.
"I think that multiple ownership between eight companies and three governments substantially lowers the risks," said Richard Matzke, president of Chevron Overseas Petroleum Inc.
A CPC source also said that a shareholders' agreement included a clause which did not allow a member to vote on any issues which might present a conflict of interest.
Matzke said Chevron was working on the assumption of financing the project with equity , but did not exclude the possibility of raising funds through investment banks.

Chevron Corp owns 15 percent of CPC, LUKoil LKOH.RTS 12.5 percent, Mobil Corp and Rosneft 7.5 percent each, Britain's BG Plc and Italy's Agip SpA two percent each, and Oryx Energy Company and Kazakhstan's Munaigaz 1.75 percent each. The remaining 50 percent is divided between Russia (24 percent), Kazakhstan (19 percent) and Oman (seven percent).
